collect.bio: Gabriel Attal (born 1989) is a Renaissance politician, a former Socialist Party member who joined Emmanuel Macron's movement in 2016. He became France's youngest Prime Minister in January 2024 and led a caretaker government after the June 2024 dissolution until September 2024. He has been Renaissance general secretary since December 2024 and chairs the Ensemble pour la République group in the Assemblée nationale. He announced his 2027 presidential candidacy on 22 May 2026.

reversals.topic: Choc des savoirs (ability-level grouping in school)
reversals.before: As Education Minister and PM (2023-2024), he launched the 'choc des savoirs' with level-based groups in collège as a flagship reform.
reversals.after: Per Wikipedia (secondary), the grouping was later abandoned as ineffective, about two years after launch. Not verified against a primary or second source. The exact formal decision and who took it (Attal or successors) are unconfirmed.

reversals.before: Attal pushed a school-uniform experiment in about 10 schools, in his Education Minister and PM period.
reversals.after: Per Wikipedia (secondary), it was abolished in summer 2026 for minimal effectiveness. The decision was taken by a later government, so it is not clearly a personal reversal by Attal.

delivery.what: Abaya and qamis ban in public schools (Education Minister, August-September 2023)
delivery.assessment: Presented as a secularism measure. Per Wikipedia, left-wing parties and Muslim councils protested it. It is widely seen as a defining act of his tenure. Only one source was fetched here, so the balanced multi-outlet assessment requested is missing.

delivery.what: Short premiership (9 January to 16 July 2024, then caretaker until 5 September 2024)
delivery.assessment: He led a compact 15-member government, later 35, which included many former LR/UMP figures. Wikipedia notes he left office saying there was too little time to see his plans through. The coalition scored about 20% in the first round of the June 2024 legislative election.

The left criticised the suspension and modification of the Ecophyto pesticide-reduction plan and budget cuts to environmental programmes. This is only the critics' framing. No government or right-leaning rebuttal was retrieved.

delivery.what: Choc des savoirs and school uniform experiment
delivery.assessment: Both were launched under his authority. Per Wikipedia, the grouping and the uniform experiment were later abandoned or ended. Delivery is therefore contested and unverified.

collect.sources_note:
The WebSearch budget (200 per session) was exhausted before any search ran, so the profile rests on only three pages. These are fr.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gabriel_Attal, en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gabriel_Attal and the campaign site attalpresident.fr. The Wikipedia page on his government had an empty actions section.

Campaign site, from the fetch summary. Priorities listed:
- education ("the mother of battles")
- work and wages
- borders
- artificial intelligence
- state debt
- ecological debt

It also mentions:
- a public consultation to shape the programme
- a Lyon meeting on 10 October 2026

No detailed measures were retrieved.

Legal: the fetched Wikipedia text mentions no judicial case, so the list is empty. This is absence of evidence from limited sources, not a verified clean record. The only incident found was the 2018 outing, which was not a legal matter.

Other limits:
- The reversals list is thin and only weakly sourced.
- Traits and media portrayal are mostly unfilled.
- Key records were not checked: assurance chômage, the immigration law, pension votes, the 49.3 vote on the 2024 budget and the public-finances record. A rerun with more search budget is recommended.

Bias caveat: all content is secondary and Wikipedia-derived, plus the candidate's own site.

verify.bio: Gabriel Attal (born 16 March 1989) is a Renaissance politician who started on the Socialist side and later joined Emmanuel Macron's movement. He held several government posts from 2018 and became France's youngest Prime Minister on 9 January 2024. President Macron accepted his resignation on 16 July 2024, after the June-July 2024 snap legislative elections. He then ran a caretaker government until Michel Barnier was appointed on 5 September 2024. He has chaired the Ensemble pour la République group in the Assemblée nationale since July 2024 and has been Renaissance general secretary since December 2024. He announced his 2027 presidential candidacy on 22 May 2026 in Mur-de-Barrez (Aveyron).

offices.office: Secretary of State to the Minister of National Education and Youth
Deputy, Hauts-de-Seine 10th constituency (second term, gave up the seat to stay in government)
Minister of National Education and Youth
Prime Minister (resignation accepted 16 July 2024, caretaker until 5 September 2024)

delivery.what: Abaya and qamis ban in public schools (Education Minister, announced late August 2023, applied from the September 2023 school start)
delivery.assessment: The government presented it as a secularism (laïcité) measure. According to Wikipedia, 67 pupils were refused entry at the school start. Left-wing parties and Muslim organisations objected. It is often cited as a defining act of his time at Education. Only encyclopedic sources were checked, so this lacks a multi-outlet assessment from different leanings.

delivery.what: 'Choc des savoirs' education reform, announced December 2023 (including level-based groups in 6e and 5e) and a school-uniform experiment in about 10 schools, announced autumn 2023
delivery.assessment: Both were launched under his authority as Education Minister and then as PM. According to Wikipedia, the level-based groups were dropped about two years later as ineffective and the uniform experiment was abandoned in summer 2026. Later governments made both decisions. No primary or second source was found for the outcome, so the result is reported only, without a verdict.

delivery.what: Premiership (9 January - 16 July 2024, then caretaker until 5 September 2024)
delivery.assessment: He started with a 15-member government on 11 January 2024, which grew to 35 members on 8 February 2024. Several ministers had served under Nicolas Sarkozy or came from UMP/LR. English Wikipedia says many outlets called it the most right-leaning cabinet of Macron's tenure. Ensemble came third with 20.0% in the first round of the 30 June 2024 legislative elections. Attal later said eight months had been too little time to see his plans through.

delivery.what: Agricultural and environmental decisions as PM (early 2024)
delivery.assessment: According to English Wikipedia, his government suspended and then modified the Ecophyto pesticide-reduction plan after pressure from farmers, and cut environmental budget lines including the Green Fund. Environmental groups and the left criticised these moves. No statement of the government's rationale and no source from another leaning was retrieved, so this is one-sided.

media_portrayal.left_media: Not researched: no left-leaning outlet could be consulted. Wikipedia reports that the left criticised the abaya ban and the 2024 environmental rollbacks.
media_portrayal.right_media: Not researched: no right-leaning outlet could be consulted.
media_portrayal.neutral_media: Not researched beyond encyclopedic summaries. English Wikipedia reports that early in his premiership he was described as one of France's most popular politicians.

verify.sources_note:
Both the original research and this verification pass ran with the WebSearch budget exhausted, so no news outlet was reached. Five pages were checked:
- fr.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gabriel_Attal
- en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gabriel_Attal
- fr.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gouvernement_Gabriel_Attal
- his Assemblée nationale page (assemblee-nationale.fr/dyn/deputes/PA722190), which confirms his current seat and his role as EPR group president
- the campaign site attalpresident.fr

The campaign site uses the slogan "La force d'agir". It sets out four themes:
- reducing the debt
- education and youth
- removing obstacles to growth
- fairness between generations

It also announces a Lyon meeting on 10 October 2026.

Legal: no judicial case appears in the sources checked. This shows only that none was found in limited sources; it does not prove a clean record.

Not covered:
- reversals, traits and media portrayal
- assurance chômage, the immigration law, pension votes and the public-finances record

Bias caveat: all content comes from secondary encyclopedic sources plus the candidate's own site. A rerun with a search budget and outlets of different leanings is needed before publishing.
